openingBell.title: The Opening Bell
openingBell.intro: Thursday, Jupiter's day (Thor's day in the old north). Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold. Jupiter is the king's planet: abundance, generosity, a full table. Breathe like you already have enough, then go take more ground.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds squares the mind. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then go build.

mindset.body: The Bears and Lions both had three days to get ready. Nobody gets extra time today, so the edge goes to whoever prepared before they had to. Same for you: a holiday isn't a day off from who you are. Get your reps in early, be fully present with your people, and still go to bed a little sharper than you woke up. Competitive. Unbeatable. Always rising. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Thursday, Jupiter's day. Earn the feast: three blocks, no rest between.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom's RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

Thursday belongs to Jupiter (jeudi in French) and to Thor in the Germanic calendar. Jupiter rules expansion, generosity and good fortune: a fitting planet for a feast day.

The Greek word for thanksgiving, eucharistia, became the name of the central Christian rite. In the Gnostic Gospel of Philip, gratitude is part of the soul's return: what you receive with thanks becomes your own.
The 13th-century Sufi poet wrote that a human being is a guest house, and every arrival, joy or sorrow, should be met at the door 'laughing' and treated honorably. Welcome the whole day.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.source: From the wisdom attributed to Solomon
grimoire.body: Solomon wrote: 'A merry heart doeth good like a medicine: but a broken spirit drieth the bones' (Proverbs 17:22). Joy isn't a soft extra. It's fuel, and you can choose it on purpose.
grimoire.practice: At the table today, say one specific thing you're grateful for out loud, then name one person who made this year better and tell them.
